papers.title: Rethinking Embodied Navigation via Relational Inductive Bias
papers.summary: Object navigation requires an agent to locate a target in an unknown environment through visual observations. Existing methods typically rely on open-vocabulary detectors or vision-language models (VLMs) to answer where to search, but often overlook what not to trust - which semantic cues are unreliable. Open-vocabulary perception is prone to systematic misleading evidence: false positives, outdated static priors, and repeated failed exploration due to lack of embodied verification, which contaminates mapping and decision-making. Such errors are rooted in structured object relations in real-world scenes. To address this, we propose DB-Nav, a framework that reshapes the search space via dual relational biases. It factorizes target-centric relations into an Activation Bias (propagates contextual evidence) and an Inhibition Bias (suppresses unreliable regions via perceptual confusion and action-level falsification). These biases are unified into a Relational Activation-Inhibition Exploration Graph that modulates frontier exploration values using online observations and failed accesses. Experiments on ObjectNav benchmarks show that DB-Nav significantly outperforms existing methods in success rate (SR) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL), offering a lightweight, interpretable, and robust navigation framework without costly online VLM reasoning.

openclaw.abstract_zh: ObjectNav 要求智能体在未知环境中通过视觉观测定位目标。现有方法通常依赖开放词汇检测器或视觉语言模型判断去哪里搜索，但常忽略哪些语义线索不可信。开放词汇感知容易产生系统性误导证据，包括假阳性、过时静态先验，以及缺少具身验证导致的重复失败探索，从而污染地图构建和决策。这些错误源于真实场景中的结构化物体关系。为此，论文提出 DB-Nav，通过双重关系偏置重塑搜索空间。它将目标中心关系分解为激活偏置和抑制偏置，前者传播上下文证据，后者通过感知混淆和动作级证伪抑制不可靠区域。这些偏置被统一到关系激活-抑制探索图中，并利用在线观测和失败访问调制前沿探索价值。ObjectNav 基准实验显示，DB-Nav 在 SR 和 SPL 上显著优于现有方法，提供了轻量、可解释、鲁棒且无需昂贵在线 VLM 推理的导航框架。

papers.title: AllDayNav: Lifelong Navigation via Real-World Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Lifelong embodied navigation in dynamic environments requires robots to form persistent scene understanding from fragmentary observations, which remains difficult for existing methods that rely on explicit maps or scene graphs and struggle to generalize beyond structured settings. We propose AllDayNav, a lifelong self-learning navigation framework that implicitly encodes scene dynamics into the billion-scale parameters of a large model via reinforcement learning, powered by a self-evolving multimodal memory that maintains and updates visual keyframes, semantic descriptions, and temporal context while autonomously generating open-vocabulary instructions, image goals, and structured rewards. Experiments in both synthetic and real-world environments across cross-room, cross-episode, and cross-task scenarios show that AllDayNav achieves success rates approaching $100\%$ and consistently surpasses strong map-based, VLM, and RL baselines in path efficiency and robustness, demonstrating implicit, memory-driven reinforcement learning as a scalable alternative to explicit mapping for reliable lifelong navigation.

papers.title: GUIDE: Goal-Initialized Directional Understanding for End-to-End Visual Navigation
papers.summary: Learning-based visual navigation for legged robots typically relies on continuous goal updates from hierarchical state estimation to provide a persistent directional reference. This reliance incurs additional sensory and computational overhead and deviates from fully end-to-end mobile autonomy. Furthermore, under partial observability, policies are prone to learn myopic behaviors, easily becoming trapped in dead ends and complex structural layouts. To address these limitations, we investigate a goal-initialized navigation setting, where the target is provided only once at the beginning of an episode, requiring the robot to operate based on intrinsic spatial memory without subsequent goal updates from external modules. In this work, we propose GUIDE, a fully end-to-end reinforcement learning framework designed to cultivate internal directional awareness. Specifically, GUIDE incorporates a spatial anchor predictor that leverages multi-frequency proprioceptive history to extract egomotion representations, thereby maintaining a persistent long-horizon spatial context for navigation. Concurrently, it utilizes raw depth streams to perceive local environmental geometry. We evaluate the proposed framework across both simulation and real-world scenarios on a quadruped robot. Experiments show that GUIDE learns reliable egomotion and directional awareness, enabling a fully end-to-end deployed policy to safely navigate through dense clutter and structured mazes without subsequent goal guidance or prior maps.

openclaw.solved_problem_zh: 这篇论文解决了腿式机器人视觉导航中依赖持续目标更新和外部状态估计的问题，并缓解部分可观测下策略容易短视、陷入死胡同或复杂结构布局的导航困难。

openclaw.relevance_zh: 该工作与具身智能导航高度相关，聚焦机器人视觉导航、强化学习策略、空间记忆、方向感知和无先验地图的真实四足机器人导航。
openclaw.problem_zh: 学习式视觉导航通常需要分层状态估计持续提供目标方向参考，带来额外传感和计算开销，也不符合完全端到端自主导航；在部分可观测环境中，策略还容易学习短视行为，在密集杂物、死胡同和结构化迷宫中失败。

openclaw.contribution_zh: 核心贡献是提出目标初始化导航设定和GUIDE框架，使四足机器人在没有后续目标引导和先验地图的情况下，通过内部方向意识与空间记忆实现端到端视觉导航。

openclaw.abstract_zh: 面向腿式机器人的学习式视觉导航通常依赖分层状态估计持续更新目标，以提供稳定方向参考，但这会增加传感和计算开销，也偏离完全端到端移动自主。在部分可观测条件下，策略容易短视，并陷入死胡同或复杂结构布局。为解决这些问题，论文研究目标初始化导航：目标只在回合开始提供一次，机器人之后必须依靠内部空间记忆而非外部模块的后续目标更新运行。论文提出GUIDE，一个完全端到端强化学习框架，用于培养内部方向意识。GUIDE包含空间锚点预测器，利用多频率本体感知历史提取自运动表征，从而维持长时程空间上下文；同时利用原始深度流感知局部环境几何。论文在仿真和真实四足机器人场景中评估该框架，实验表明GUIDE能学习可靠的自运动和方向意识，使端到端部署的策略在没有后续目标引导或先验地图的情况下安全穿越密集杂物和结构化迷宫。

papers.title: GuideWalk: Learning Unified Autonomous Navigation and Locomotion for Humanoid Robots across Versatile Terrains
papers.summary: Humanoid robots have achieved strong locomotion capabilities, but reliable navigation on versatile terrains remains challenging because obstacle avoidance must be coordinated with dynamically feasible motion. In this work, we present GuideWalk, a unified end-to-end framework that integrates traversability-aware navigation guidance with terrain-adaptive locomotion teacher for humanoid navigation. Specifically, we introduce a navigation module that provides explicit velocity guidance, decoupling obstacle avoidance from terrain conditions to enable robust planning across diverse environments. We propose a composite teacher distillation scheme, where goal-directed commands and dynamically consistent actions are aggregated and distilled into a single policy. To further improve robustness, the distilled policy is refined with reinforcement learning and an auxiliary behavior cloning objective, which promotes exploration while preserving desirable teacher behaviors. Experiments demonstrate that GuideWalk achieves stable and effective navigation while maintaining stable humanoid locomotion.

papers.title: AgenticNav: Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation as a Tool-Calling Harness
papers.summary: Zero-shot vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments (VLN-CE) has recently become feasible with large vision-language models (VLMs). However, existing methods typically rely on learned waypoint predictors to propose navigable actions. This severely limits the model's action space and fails to leverage depth inputs effectively. Moreover, memory is commonly handled by accumulating long textual or visual histories with substantial irrelevant context, or by retrieving cross-episode experiences, which weakens the zero-shot setting. In this paper, we rethink zero-shot VLN-CE as an agentic interface between the VLM and the environment, and present AgenticNav, a lightweight navigation harness that exposes action, depth, and memory as callable tools. Instead of choosing from predicted waypoints, the action tool allows the VLM to directly select a target pixel in RGB observations, converting it into executable motion. Depth is exposed through an on-demand pixel-depth tool, enabling the VLM to request precise metric distances only where they matter. For memory, AgenticNav provides a compact map image summarizing the historical trajectory, paired with a recall tool that allows the VLM to selectively revisit past visual observations without overwhelming the prompt context. On the R2R-CE benchmark, AgenticNav establishes new state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance among zero-shot methods given the same VLM backbone. Real-world validation further highlights its zero-shot generalization compared to prior methods. Ablations show that our action tool design outperforms traditional waypoint predictors, and that depth tool and agentic memory further contribute to navigation performance.

papers.title: AgniNav: Configuration-Driven Cross-Embodiment Local Planning for Robot Navigation
papers.summary: Monocular local navigation is attractive for lightweight robots, but existing vision-based policies often couple perception to a specific body, camera height, and footprint, making transfer from wheeled bases to legged platforms dependent on retraining or active depth hardware. This paper introduces AgniNav, a configuration-driven local navigation framework that standardizes cross-embodiment transfer at the collision-envelope level. Each robot is specified by a measurable four-parameter safety envelope: collision-relevant height, front length, rear length, and half width. The height parameter conditions an image-to-scan network to predict a one-dimensional, collision-relevant pseudo-laserscan from a monocular color image, while the remaining footprint parameters configure a dimension-aware local planner for collision checking. Training uses height-conditioned column-minimum scan labels generated from paired color-depth data, allowing the same image to supervise different safety envelopes without collecting robot-specific data. To the best of our knowledge, AgniNav is the first monocular local-navigation framework that jointly conditions perception and planning on a shared collision-envelope configuration for zero-retraining deployment across wheeled, quadruped, and humanoid platforms. Real-robot experiments on a Turtlebot2, Unitree Go2, and Accelerated Evolution K1 achieve 39/40, 18/20, and 18/20 successes with 0/40, 1/20, and 2/20 collisions, respectively, while running at 30 Hz on Jetson Orin.

papers.title: Act on What You See: Unlocking Safe Social Navigation in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: Safe social navigation requires robots to distinguish people from ordinary obstacles and to react before danger becomes imminent. We show that pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models already encode pedestrian-object distinctions and future collision signals in their internal representations, but behavior cloning fails to translate these signals into socially appropriate actions. To address this mismatch, we propose SALSA, a two-stage annotation-free post-training framework: (1) social behavioral alignment bridges intermediate-layer social features to the action head and trains on counterfactual human-object scene pairs to break visual saliency shortcuts; (2) temporal safety alignment provides automatically generated future-risk supervision to enable anticipatory collision avoidance. On SCAND and real-world deployment, SALSA reduces near-collisions by 86.4% and improves social counterfactual accuracy from 53% to 93%, demonstrating that safer social navigation can be achieved by teaching VLA policies to act on representations they already possess. These results show that pretrained VLA policies can be adapted for safer social navigation by better aligning their latent representations with action generation.

openclaw.title_zh: 看见什么就对什么行动：释放视觉-语言-动作模型中的安全社交导航能力
openclaw.solved_problem_zh: 这篇论文解决了预训练视觉-语言-动作模型虽然内部已有行人与物体区分和未来碰撞信号，但行为克隆无法把这些信号转化为安全社交导航动作的问题。
openclaw.tldr_zh: 论文提出 SALSA，让 VLA 机器人策略更好利用已有视觉表征，提前避开行人并减少近碰撞。
openclaw.relevance_zh: 与机器人社交导航和具身智能导航高度相关，重点在 VLA 策略如何区分行人与普通障碍物，并进行面向未来风险的安全动作生成。
openclaw.problem_zh: 安全社交导航要求机器人区分人和普通障碍物，并在危险临近前提前反应；摘要指出现有行为克隆不能充分利用 VLA 模型内部已有的社交特征和碰撞风险信号。
openclaw.method_zh: 提出两阶段、无需标注的后训练框架 SALSA：先进行社交行为对齐，把中间层社交特征连接到动作头，并用反事实人-物场景对打破视觉显著性捷径；再进行时间安全对齐，用自动生成的未来风险监督训练提前避碰。
openclaw.contribution_zh: 核心贡献是证明预训练 VLA 策略中已有行人-物体区分和未来碰撞信号，并通过 SALSA 将这些潜在表征更好对齐到动作生成，从而提升安全社交导航表现。
key_contributions_zh: 提出无需人工标注的两阶段后训练框架 SALSA，用于安全社交导航
通过社交行为对齐和反事实人-物场景对，提升 VLA 对行人与物体的动作区分能力
通过时间安全对齐引入自动生成的未来风险监督，实现更具预判性的碰撞避免
openclaw.experiments_zh: 摘要说明在 SCAND 和真实世界部署中评估，SALSA 将近碰撞减少 86.4%，并将社交反事实准确率从 53% 提升到 93%。
openclaw.limitations_zh: 摘要未说明，需要看正文核验。
openclaw.read_suggestion_zh: 建议关注其反事实人-物场景构造、未来风险监督生成方式，以及这些对齐方法是否可迁移到 VLN、ObjectNav、PointNav 或更复杂机器人导航场景。
openclaw.abstract_zh: 安全社交导航要求机器人区分人和普通障碍物，并在危险临近前做出反应。作者发现，预训练 VLA 模型的内部表征已经包含行人与物体的区分信息和未来碰撞信号，但行为克隆无法将这些信号转化为合适的社交导航动作。为此，论文提出 SALSA，一个两阶段、无需标注的后训练框架：第一阶段进行社交行为对齐，将中间层社交特征连接到动作头，并利用反事实人-物场景对打破视觉显著性捷径；第二阶段进行时间安全对齐，通过自动生成的未来风险监督，使机器人能够提前避免碰撞。在 SCAND 和真实世界部署中，SALSA 将近碰撞减少 86.4%，并将社交反事实准确率从 53% 提升到 93%。结果表明，通过更好地对齐潜在表征与动作生成，预训练 VLA 策略可以适配到更安全的社交导航。

papers.title: Resilient Navigation for Autonomous Farm Robots by Leveraging Jerk-Augmented Models with IMU-Only Disturbance Rejection
papers.summary: Precise state estimation for navigation of autonomous agricultural robots is often compromised by sensor outages (GNSS/LiDAR/Visual) and high-frequency vibrations inherent in off-road environments. This paper proposes a robust navigation algorithm based on a jerk-augmented Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) integrated with a Multiple Tuning Factor (MTF) adaptation method. Unlike standard EKF approaches that assume constant measurement noise, our method dynamically adjusts the measurement covariance matrix in real-time, allowing the system to cope with sudden disturbances and sensor outliers. We evaluate the algorithm using real-world data from a Salin247 autonomous robot. Results demonstrate that jerk-augmentation combined with MTF adaptation significantly reduces 3D position Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) compared to baseline EKF models, providing superior dead-reckoning capabilities.

openclaw.title_zh: 利用含加加速度模型与仅 IMU 扰动抑制实现自主农场机器人鲁棒导航
openclaw.solved_problem_zh: 这篇论文解决了自主农业机器人在 GNSS、LiDAR、视觉等传感器中断以及越野高频振动下，导航状态估计精度下降的问题。
openclaw.tldr_zh: 论文提出一种改进 EKF，让农场机器人在传感器异常和强振动时仍能更稳地估计位置。
openclaw.relevance_zh: 与机器人导航和状态估计高度相关，重点在农业越野场景中的鲁棒导航；不涉及 VLN、ObjectNav、PointNav、地图构建、场景图或语言空间推理。
openclaw.problem_zh: 自主农业机器人在非结构化越野环境中容易遇到 GNSS、LiDAR、视觉传感器失效或异常，同时车体高频振动会干扰状态估计，导致导航定位不可靠。
openclaw.method_zh: 方法基于加入 jerk 的扩展卡尔曼滤波器，并结合多调谐因子自适应方法，实时调整测量协方差矩阵，以应对突发扰动和传感器离群值。
openclaw.contribution_zh: 论文的核心贡献是将 jerk 增广状态模型与 MTF 自适应测量噪声调节结合，用于提升农业机器人在传感器异常和强扰动下的惯性/航位推算导航能力。
key_contributions_zh: 提出 jerk-augmented EKF 用于鲁棒导航状态估计
引入 MTF 自适应机制实时调整测量协方差矩阵
基于 Salin247 自主机器人真实数据验证并降低 3D 位置 RMSE
openclaw.experiments_zh: 摘要说明使用 Salin247 自主机器人真实世界数据进行评估，并与基线 EKF 模型比较，结果显示 3D 位置 RMSE 显著降低，航位推算能力更强。
openclaw.limitations_zh: 摘要未说明，需要看正文核验。
openclaw.read_suggestion_zh: 建议关注其 jerk 增广 EKF 状态建模、MTF 协方差自适应策略，以及在传感器中断场景下的 dead-reckoning 评估设置；若研究视觉导航、语义地图或 VLN，可作为底层鲁棒定位模块参考。
openclaw.abstract_zh: 自主农业机器人的精确导航状态估计常受到 GNSS、LiDAR、视觉传感器中断以及越野环境高频振动影响。本文提出一种鲁棒导航算法，基于 jerk 增广扩展卡尔曼滤波器，并集成多调谐因子自适应方法。不同于假设测量噪声恒定的标准 EKF，该方法实时动态调整测量协方差矩阵，使系统能够应对突发扰动和传感器离群值。论文使用 Salin247 自主机器人真实世界数据进行评估，结果显示 jerk 增广与 MTF 自适应结合相比基线 EKF 显著降低 3D 位置 RMSE，并提供更好的航位推算能力。
